reports.title: Eliot Harris: Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: The ward has improved their processes which now ensures the nurse in charge is identified and roles allocated to the shift team members. To achieve this, the daily allocation form has been reviewed which clearly identifies the nurse in charge. In addition, the Matron oversees the off duty rota and delegates nurse- in-charge duties each shift. This is monitored by the Clinical Team Leader and Modern Matron. [name redacted] to this aspect the trust is formulating a seminar on shift co-ordination and
promises.summary: Improved shift coordination and role allocation

concerns.quote: Substantial evidence was heard at the inquest with regard to observations which were not carried out in respect of Eliot Harris in accordance with NSFT's Policy and with regard to staff not undergoing training and assessment of their competency to carry out observations correctly.
On the night of Eliot's death, a Nurse in Charge had not been allocated and members of staff were not allocated specific tasks - they were told to
Multi Team Meetings were not fully and properly recorded in the clinical records
Eliot's Care Plan was not up to date at the time of his death
Staff were reluctant to enter Eliot's room following concern for his wellbeing
It is not clear from the evidence what is now in place to ensure that relevant and requested physical health checks are carried out

reports.title: Ellen Woolnough: Prevention of future deaths report

promises.quote: The Trust has recently been reviewing and updating their Clinical Risk Assessment and Management Policy. This Policy is currently progressing through Trust internal governance processes and is due to be published end of June 2024, with a Policy implementation plan to be progressed during July/August 2024.
promises.summary: Review and update Clinical Risk Assessment and Management Policy

concerns.quote: The adequacy of Norfolk and Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust's (NSFT) Integrated Delivery Team (IDT) decision making concerning the discharge of a patient from mental health services in circumstances where a failed engagement has occurred
concerns.hazard: discharge of patient from mental health services with failed engagement

concerns.quote: The adequacy of NSFT's Crisis Rehabilitation Home Treatment Team (CRHTT) response to an urgent referral, in particular; risk assessment, safety planning and decision making concerning the downgrading of referrals
Adequacy of the NHS England Patient Safety Incident Response Framework (PSIRF) to address serious incidents concerning patients and the implementation of this framework by NSFT

The failure by NSFT to preserve important evidence, in the form of recordings of calls between Ellie and the NSFT crisis call handler, at a time when it was on notice that this evidence would be important and relevant for the conduct of the Inquest

reports.title: Nigel Hammond: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

concerns.quote: I am concerned, as had the AHMP in Nigel's case been able to directly refer him to the Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team on the 9th March 2024, mental health professionals would have attended, and been able to provide additional support, advice and potentially additional treatment for Nigel, in all likelihood preventing his death.
concerns.hazard: lack of direct referral to crisis team

links.explanation: Both reports concern problems with accessing the Crisis Rehabilitation/Home Treatment Team (CRHTT) – one focuses on the adequacy of the team's response to urgent referrals, the other on barriers preventing direct referral by approved mental health professionals.
links.earlier_quote: The adequacy of NSFT's Crisis Rehabilitation Home Treatment Team (CRHTT) response to an urgent referral, in particular; risk assessment, safety planning and decision making concerning the downgrading of referrals.
links.later_quote: However, the court was told that an AMHP, despite their role in the coordination of the mental health assessment and admission to hospital of a patient, were not permitted to make direct referrals to the emergency Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight problems with ensuring timely physical health checks for patients with mental health needs. The earlier report notes delays due to mandatory checks before referral, while the later report points out uncertainty about current processes to carry out those checks.

links.later_quote: It is not clear from the evidence what is now in place to ensure that relevant and requested physical health checks are carried out

links.explanation: Both reports highlight a barrier that prevents mental health professionals from making immediate referrals to specialist services, causing dangerous delays. The earlier barrier involves GPs needing a physical health check before referral; the later barrier involves AMHPs being unable to refer directly to the Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team.

links.later_quote: an AMHP, despite their role in the coordination of the mental health assessment and admission to hospital of a patient, were not permitted to make direct referrals to the emergency Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team.

links.explanation: Both reports highlight barriers in the referral pathway that delay or prevent timely access to the Crisis Resolution and Home Treatment Team. The earlier case shows excessive waiting times after referral; the later case shows a lack of authority to make direct referrals, causing a similar delay in crisis intervention.
